title: Tracking the growth fate of single cells and isolating slow-growing cells in human colorectal cancer organoids
protocol: Collect fresh surgical CRC sample and immediately proceed to tissue dissociation in a biological safety cabinet.
Transfer the CRC sample to a 90 mm petri dish.
Cut tumor fragment into pieces less than 2 mm using tweezers and scalpel.
Wash minced tumor fragments with 20 ml of HBSS buffer, gently mix up and down a couple of times.
Transfer washed fragments to a new 50 ml conical tube.
Discard supernatant after waiting for approximately 1 min.
Resuspend tumor fragments with 10 ml of tumor dissociation solution containing Liberase DH.
Transfer minced tumor fragment suspension to a 100 ml sterile conical flask with a magnet bar.
Incubate the sample for ∼15–30 min in a 37°C water bath with constant stirring at 700 rpm.
Add 10 μL of DNase I for the last 15 min of incubation.
Strain the suspension of digested tumor fragments using mesh filters and 50 mL conical tubes.
Pass the digested tumor suspension through a sterile stainless-steel wire mesh with hole size: 500 μm.
Transfer the flow-through into the next mesh filter.
Wash the tumor fragments trapped in the mesh with 5 mL of HBSS buffer.
Repeat these steps for each filtration step.
Use stainless-steel wire mesh with hole size: 250 μm for subsequent straining.
Pass through a 100-μm cell strainer (Falcon® Cell Strainers).
Finally, pass through a 40-μm cell strainer (Falcon® Cell Strainers).
Transfer the mesh filter containing tumor fragments to a non-treated 60 mm Petri dish.
Add 1-2 ml of CTOS organoid medium to the filter.
Scratch and collect tumor fragments using a P1000 pipette.
Proceed to step 10 after collecting tumor fragments.
Wash CRC organoids twice with HBSS buffer the day after preparation to remove cellular debris.
Collect CRC organoids and transfer into a 1.5 mL tube.
Mix the suspension up and down ten times using a P1000 pipette.
Wait approximately 1–2 minutes for the CRC organoids to settle at the bottom of the tube.
Discard the supernatant, which mainly consists of debris and/or dead cells.
Wash the CRC organoids with 1 mL of HBSS buffer.
Repeat washing steps as necessary.
Add 1 mL of CTOS organoid medium to the CRC organoids.
Transfer CRC organoids to a non-treated 6-well plate dish containing 2–3 mL of CTOS organoid medium per well.
Incubate the organoid culture in a 5% CO2-humidified chamber at 37°C for 6 days.
Monitor CRC organoid cultures daily once established.
Passage CRC organoids once a week to expand and maintain viability.
Culture CRC organoids in suspension if necessary.
Add Matrigel GFR and/or growth factors (e.g., 100 μg/mL of bFGF and/or 10 μg/mL of Rho-kinase inhibitor) to the CTOS organoid medium for some CRC lines as needed.
Embed CRC organoids in Matrigel GFR depending on their viability and growth rate.
Dissociate CRC organoids using the syringe disruption method once a week.
Collect CRC organoids one week after preparation or previous dissociation when spheroids reach 200–300 μm diameter.
Transfer CRC organoids into a 1.5 mL tube.
Mix suspension up and down ten times using a P1000 Pipette.
Wait approximately 1-2 minutes for the CRC organoids to settle at the bottom of the tube.
Discard supernatant liquid composed mainly of debris and/or dead cells.
Centrifuge CRC organoids at 400 × g for 3 min at 25°C if they do not settle at the bottom.
Wash CRC organoids with 1 mL of HBSS buffer.
Repeat centrifugation and washing steps as necessary.
Add 200 μL of CTOS organoid medium to the CRC organoids.
Disrupt CRC organoids into smaller fragments by passing them through a 1 mL syringe with a 27 G needle at ∼0.5 mL/s for 5–10 times.
Resuspend disrupted CRC organoids in a non-treated 6-well plate containing 2–3 mL of CTOS organoid medium per well.
Incubate the culture in a 5% CO2-humidified chamber at 37°C for 1 week.
Replace the medium once every 3–4 days as standard.
Swirl the plate clockwise if organoids are in suspension to gather them at the center.
Aspirate old medium from the edge of the plate using a P1000 pipette.
Replace aspirated medium with fresh medium.
Pellet organoids using centrifugation at 400 × g for 3 min at 25°C if necessary.
After pelleting, aspirate old medium carefully and resuspend organoids in freshly prepared medium.
Subject CRC organoids to further experiments at least one day after passaging.
Culture and expand organoids from freshly harvested primary CRC tumors for 2–3 weeks before SSFG assay.
Freeze-stock organoids with StemCell Keep according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Transfer one hundred to a thousand CRC organoids into a 15 mL conical tube containing 10 mL of HBSS buffer.
Centrifuge the CRC organoids at 400 × g for 3 min at 25°C.
Discard the supernatant and wash the organoid pellet with 10 mL of HBSS buffer.
Centrifuge the CRC organoids at 400 × g for 3 min at 25°C, then discard the supernatant.
Add 2 mL of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA to the organoid pellet.
Mix the suspension up and down ten times using a P1000 pipette.
Incubate the mixture for ∼5–10 min at 37°C in a water bath.
Gently pipette the cell suspension a hundred times to promote organoid dissociation into single cells.
Add 6 mL of CTOS organoid medium to inactivate trypsin.
Add 8 μL of DNase I (10 μg/mL) and incubate for 1 min at 25°C.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400 × g for 3 min at 25°C.
Discard the supernatant liquid and wash the cell pellet with 10 mL of HBSS buffer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400 × g for 3 min at 25°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant to avoid loss of the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of HBSS buffer and filter into a 5 mL round bottom tube with a 35-μm cell strainer cap to remove cell clusters.
Keep the cell suspension on ice and determine the cell count.
Examine the single-cell status under a microscope if necessary.
Dissociate using steps 23–26 again if organoid dissociation into single cells is incomplete.
Dilute ∼300–400 cells in a 20 mL cold SSFG medium.
Keep the cell suspension on ice.
Dispense the cell suspension into a sterile reagent reservoir and gently mix.
Seed the cell suspension into a non-treated 384-well plate with a ratio of one cell per well (50 μL/well).
Centrifuge the plate at 400 × g for 3 min at 25°C.
Incubate the plate in a 5% CO2-humidified chamber at 37°C and culture for 2–3 weeks.
Confirm the presence of one cell per well within 2 h of cell seeding by image acquisition using a LEICA DMI4000B microscope equipped with Lumina Vision.
After 7 days of culture, add 30 μL of fresh SSFG medium (without Y-27632) per well using an E1-ClipTip electronic pipette and a sterile reagent reservoir.
Add the medium to the top of the 50 μL previously seeded.

At the end of the SSFG assay, pick up small spheroids and individually transfer them into a well of a non-coated 96-well plate containing 100 μL of CTOS organoid medium supplemented with 2% Matrigel GFR.
Incubate the spheroids in a 5% CO2-humidified chamber at 37°C and culture for 2 weeks.
Monitor slow-growing spheroids daily.
Change CTOS organoid medium supplemented with 2% Matrigel GFR after one week of culture.
Aspirate the old medium from the top using a P200 pipette carefully without aspirating or losing the spheroids.
Add fresh medium to each well.
Dissociate slow-growing spheroids reaching a size of 3–4 × 105 μm² by syringe disruption method.
Culture disrupted spheroids (one clone per well) in 500 μL CTOS organoid medium with 2% Matrigel GFR into a well of non-coated 24-well plate.
Incubate the spheroids in a 5% CO₂-humidified chamber at 37°C for 1 week.
Perform subsequent rounds of SSFG assay to confirm slow-growing pattern after isolating the slow-growing spheroids.
